newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Chairman Oscar Wyatt to step down.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Chairman Oscar Wyatt to step down.

text.p: Oscar Wyatt, founder and chairman of Coastal Corp., said Tuesday he planned to retire as chairman as of July 15 but will remain on the international oil and natural gas company's board of directors.
Wyatt will be succeeded by President and Chief Executive David Arledge, who will retain his current roles.
Wyatt, who founded Coastal more than 40 years ago and has served as its only chairman, will remain on the board and as chairman of its executive committee, the company said.

"At this particular stage of Coastal's growth and expansion, I think it is incumbent on me to make room for the advancement of younger executives," Wyatt said in a statement. "I am pleased with Coastal's progress and am very optimistic about its future."
Coastal is a Houston-based holding company with consolidated assets of more than $11 billion.
Its stock rose 87.5 cents to $47.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
